_comment: Sales Engagement's prompt registry — the fourth module to own one, and it owns it for the reason the other three do: a module owns its own artifacts (CLAUDE.md §2). `load_prompt_registry(directory)` is already per-directory, so no platform change was needed. `fingerprint` is the SHA-256 of name, version and text; the loader refuses to start if the file disagrees with it. A released version is never edited in place — a change is a new version. `evaluations` is append-only, outside the fingerprint, and is written by `make eval-approach`, never by hand. **`rendering_protocol_version` on a Sales Engagement evaluation names the Commercial Context Protocol** (`domain/context.py`), not the AI Platform's evidence rendering protocol — these prompts are shown a reasoning graph and never an evidence set. That divergence is C-214, and until it is answered this module derives its own release eligibility in `sales_engagement/domain/release.py` rather than through `PromptVersion.is_released`, which would compare against the wrong constant. **The one evaluation on record is a failing run, and it is here deliberately** — a manifest holding only passes would show a prompt with a clean history and no way to see it had been measured and found wanting, and the next engineer would repeat the work. `executive_summary@1` is therefore **measured and unreleased**: one of ten cases was refused, so no pairing is earned. Release is earned, never declared.
